requirements.title: Provider selection and storefront display
requirements.description: The user can choose a commerce provider from a list of supported providers that have their own compatible templates. When a user selects a provider, they are taken to that provider's specific repository or demo site, allowing them to see a working storefront tailored to that commerce backend.
requirements.userAction: User clicks on a commerce provider link from the list of providers.
requirements.expectedOutcome: User is redirected to the selected provider's repository or demo site, showing a storefront built with that provider's template.

requirements.title: Provider integration via fork and swap
requirements.description: For providers not officially maintained by Vercel, the user can fork the main Shopify repository and replace the lib/shopify file with their own commerce provider implementation. The rest of the template remains mostly unchanged, enabling a custom provider setup.
requirements.userAction: User forks the repository and swaps the lib/shopify file with their provider's implementation.
requirements.expectedOutcome: The user's storefront runs with their custom provider while reusing the rest of the template code.

requirements.title: Orama Integration for Enhanced Search
requirements.description: When Orama is integrated, the site search is upgraded to include typeahead with dynamic re-rendering, vector-based similarity search, and JavaScript-based configuration. For smaller catalogs, the search runs entirely in the browser; for larger catalogs, it runs on a CDN.
requirements.userAction: The user types in the search field and receives typeahead suggestions with dynamic re-rendering.
requirements.expectedOutcome: The search results show relevant, vector-based similarity matches configured via JavaScript.

requirements.title: React Bricks Visual Editing
requirements.description: With the React Bricks integration, users can visually edit pages, product details, and footer content using the React Bricks headless CMS. This allows for on-page editing without needing to modify code.
requirements.userAction: The user navigates to the storefront and uses React Bricks' visual editing interface to modify content.
requirements.expectedOutcome: The pages, product details, and footer update in real-time as the user edits, reflecting the changes visually.
